messages:
incident-bot: [SEV2] ILB healthcheck failures observed for Private VPCs in europe region. 20% request errors, spike at 12:14 UTC. Auto-pager triggered -> @sre-oncall :rotating_light:

sre-oncall: seeing high 5xx from ilb control-plane to authz proxy (third-party). Errors look like 403/429 bursts. Confirming impact: several Private VPC customers report increased latency + failed deployments.

ana: paging in — I’m on it. quick question: is traffic failing at the ILB or earlier in the auth proxy?

kevin: from logs, ILB healthchecks success -> backend auth calls start failing. stack traces show `oauth-exchange` errors and `rate_limited` from vendor. paste logs:```
[12:13:57] authz: token_exchange failed status=429 body={"error":"rate_limit"}
[12:14:02] ilb: backend_stream_closed code=500
```

liz: customers affected: cust-a, cust-b (EU), cust-c (multi-region private). Cust-b open ticket already. Not all requests fail — looks like sampling, likely third-party throttling.

mike: adding context: earlier today we rolled a minor HMAC change to healthcheck headers for Private VPC auth. Could be coincidental but worth confirming.

eng-runtime: confirmed we did a header tweak at 09:40 UTC but only for internal canaries. ILB config unchanged. Vendor is Google-managed auth proxy (third-party).

ana: mitigation plan options: 1) fall back ILB -> use internal unauthenticated healthcheck path (short term), 2) route impacted customer clusters to hosted fallback pool (may increase latency/cost), 3) ask vendor to raise rate limit (slow). Which do we prefer?

kevin: prefer 1 + 2. Do 1 ASAP to stop paging. We already have a config flag `ilb.healthcheck.auth_required` we can flip per-vpc.

liz: I'll prepare customer comms for cust-b and cust-c with note we are investigating and applying mitigations.

ana: performing handoff to @kevin for the toggle. Kevin, once you flip, monitor error rate and trace volume.

kevin: doing toggle now for cust-b and cust-c (patched via console):
```bash
# toggle auth_required -> false for VPCs
redwoodctl vpc update --id=vpc-cust-b --set ilb.healthcheck.auth_required=false
redwoodctl vpc update --id=vpc-cust-c --set ilb.healthcheck.auth_required=false
```

kevin: toggled at 12:20 UTC. Rolling healthcheck change; may take up to 30s to propagate.

pagerduty-bot: @sre-oncall acknowledged the INCIDENT (SEV2). Next update in 15m or when mitigated.

ana: initial metrics: 12:21 -> 12:27 error rate for those VPCs down from 18% -> 2%. ILB 5xx dropped significantly. Good.

mike: can we also enable hosted-fallback for cust-c to remove dependency while vendor is investigated? That needs approval from accounts-eng for potential cost delta.

accounts-eng: approved temporary hosted-fallback for cust-c for up to 4 hours. Please annotate bill impact and set TTL.

eng-runtime: we requested vendor (third-party auth) via support channel at 12:15 UTC — ticket #AUTH-1247. They confirm elevated request rates from our service and are investigating token exchange throttles.

kevin: enabling hosted-fallback for cust-c now (route policy change):
```json
{"vpc_id":"vpc-cust-c","fallback":"hosted-pool-eu","ttl":"4h","note":"temp fallback due to third-party auth rate limit"}
```

kevin: routing change applied at 12:29 UTC. Starting traffic shift.

liz: customer comms sent to cust-b and cust-c: short note + mitigation steps + rough ETA for rollback when vendor confirms resolution.

ana: secondary mitigation: increase retry/backoff on authx calls from 100ms -> 500ms jittered to reduce hammering vendor. eng-runtime can we push a config?

eng-runtime: pushing a config change to the auth-client pool now (hot config):
```yaml
auth_client:
  retry:
    base_delay_ms: 500
    max_attempts: 5
    jitter: true
```

eng-runtime: config live at 12:33 UTC. Monitoring for error rate changes.

mike: any indication vendor might throttle us indefinitely? What's their SLA?

eng-runtime: vendor response (via support thread): "We've observed a burst correlating with your tokens; we've temporarily applied protective throttles. We're increasing capacity for your tenant, ETA 2-3 hours."

ana: okay, then plan is: keep fallback + authless healthchecks until vendor confirms capacity bump, then revert `ilb.healthcheck.auth_required` and disable hosted-fallback. Post-incident action: add token-exchange rate metrics and a soft-rate-limiter client-side to avoid blast.

sre-oncall: agree. I'll keep incident active. Next status update in 30 min or sooner. Please log all commands and timelines in the incident ticket.

liz: filing followup tasks:
- Ops: restore `ilb.healthcheck.auth_required` and remove hosted-fallback after vendor confirmation (owner: kevin)
- Eng-runtime: implement client-side soft limiter + metric (owner: eng-runtime)
- Support/Accounts: reconcile billing and comms (owner: accounts-eng)

kevin: note — we must ensure healthcheck flips are gated per-vpc; global flip would be risky. Added checklist in ticket.

eng-runtime: observed no regressions in other regions. Cross-region routing stabilities look good after mitigations.

sre-oncall: recording impact: 3 Private VPC customers affected, degraded request success rates (peak 20% failures) between 12:13-12:29 UTC. No data loss, increased latency and failed deploys noted. Pager duty will remain until vendor resolves.

incident-bot: Incident thread updated. Incident ticket: INC-2026-187.

ana: thanks team — handing back to oncall monitoring. I'll be available for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

kevin: will follow up on rollback once vendor confirms. closing loop later.

accounts-eng: cust-b acknowledged and appreciated quick mitigation. Will update billing note after TTL expires.

pagersduty-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors rise above 5% for 5min, re-escalate to SEV1.

sre-oncall: closing chat handoff. All actions logged in INC-2026-187. Follow-ups assigned. Good work.
